text: Harriet Tubman escaped slavery in Maryland in 1849. Instead of staying safe in the North, she went back about 13 times by the end of 1860, risking capture each time, and led about 70 people out, most of them her own family and friends. She gave directions to about 70 more who made it on their own. Years later she said of those journeys: "I never ran my train off the track and I never lost a passenger."
verification_note: Verified with caveat: facts checked by Claude against the National Park Service fact sheet, Nov 3, 2026 (it corrects the popular "300 people in 19 trips" myth); the quote's wording matches the Massachusetts Commonwealth Museum exhibit, but where and when she first said it is not confirmed
